The security review you never had time for. Offline, rule-based, and you can verify every finding yourself.

penthera.org: check your live site in a few seconds. Passive, nothing stored.

Daily notes from Penthera: x.com/penthera_org

Who builds it: Daan van der Zwaag, part-time and in the open.

How it compares: next to Snyk, Socket, Semgrep, ZAP and GitHub.

132 readable rules · 6 read-only MCP tools · 0 runtime dependencies · 0 requests past loopback in the benchmark · MIT, no telemetry

What it is

Penthera checks your app, its dependencies and your AI coding tools on your own machine. It fixes what it can, with your approval. Every finding comes from a rule you can read, with its evidence at file:line. A model may propose; a rule decides.

It is also an open R&D project. We measure every check in public and publish the results, good or bad, so you can see how far to trust it.

It finds known classes of problems, not novel ones. It does not replace a human pentester.

Start in 30 seconds

You need Node.js 22 or later. No install, no account.

Building with Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, VS Code, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, Zed, JetBrains or Kiro, or an app builder such as Lovable, Bolt, Base44, Replit or v0? Penthera in your coding tool has the setup for each.

In your terminal. Run this in your project folder:

npx penthera

It detects your setup offline, asks what to check, and gives you a grade per area and the three things to fix first. It scans your running app only after you confirm the app is yours. Nothing is committed or pushed (guided start).

Every finding carries a severity, a confidence label (confirmed, likely, potential, needs-human-review), its evidence and the research behind it. Reports come out as Markdown, JSON and SARIF for GitHub code scanning. Exit code 1 means critical or high findings. Every command and flag is in docs/commands/. Compliance output is readiness tooling, not a certification and not legal advice.

AI mode (opt-in). penthera --repo . --ai lets a local model propose problems no rule describes. Penthera checks each proposal with its rules, and anything unconfirmed is labelled "model-proposed, unverified" and never fails CI. Whether it finds more than the rules alone is not measured yet (AI mode).

How it is measured

Each feature goes through the same path: method → evidence → tool.

  • Method. The methodology states the threat model, what black-box (HTTP) and white-box (source) analysis can and cannot see, the confidence model, and the false-positive controls on each probe. Each design choice cites the research or standard it rests on: 158 verified references, in APA style, in docs/references.md.
  • Evidence. A benchmark runs on every release, and the release gate fails if precision or recall drops by more than 0.02. Experiments that decide what ships next are pre-registered in docs/research/prereg/ before any data is collected, and the results are published either way.
  • Tool. What holds up ships in a reviewed, signed release. What does not hold up is dropped, and the rules stay.

The bundled benchmark is 24 findings in small labs we wrote ourselves. It catches regressions; it does not measure real-world accuracy. The E10 pilot used one labeller and is not independent: the fixes were written after seeing the misses on the same two apps. On WebGoat, held out, recall stayed at 2 of 9. Accuracy on real projects is experiment E1, pre-registered and not yet run. Intervals are Wilson. What Penthera cannot see is listed under Known limitations. Why you can trust it

  • Local and offline. No account, no telemetry, no cloud. --offline limits network traffic to the target you named, and every report lists the hosts it contacted (network use).
  • Tested unplugged. Repo scans, agents, deps, brief, evidence bundles and URL scans with --offline made no outside connections. They gave the same result twice, and the same with the network blocked, on macOS and Ubuntu (E17 results). The test can't watch git, which Penthera uses only for local commands.
  • Deterministic. Rules you can read, with file:line evidence. A model may propose a fix or a lead; a deterministic re-scan and your tests decide.
  • Non-destructive by default. Default scans send no attack payloads. Payload testing (--deep, --fuzz, --adaptive, --all) is opt-in, asks for a confirmation bound to the target, and is rate-limited. It can change data, so read what active modes can change first.
  • Asks before it changes anything. The fix loop works on a local branch, asks before every change by default, and never pushes or opens pull requests.
  • No update channel to hijack. Detection rules ship inside reviewed releases as signed, versioned rule packs. You can add your own by path (--rules <dir>). Nothing is downloaded and run at run time.
  • Releases you can verify. npm provenance through trusted publishing, a maintainer approval with 2FA for every version, SHA-pinned CI, CodeQL and OpenSSF Scorecard. Every release passes an internal audit of eight gates (latest report).

The claim map ties these claims to the tests that hold them.

Verify it yourself. In an empty folder:

npm install penthera@2.3.2 && npm audit signatures
npx penthera@2.3.2 rules list

The first checks npm's registry signature and the build provenance of the package you got. The second lists every bundled rule pack and the key that signed it; a pack whose signature does not verify is refused unless you pass --allow-unsigned-rules.

Penthera finds known classes of problems, not novel ones, and it does not replace a human pentester or incident response. The decisions behind it, its limits, and how to challenge them are in the manifesto and FAQ.

Run the free tools you already have: --giants

--giants runs the free scanners installed on your machine after Penthera's own scan: gitleaks, TruffleHog, Semgrep with your local rules, osv-scanner, Trivy and Checkov for a repository, nuclei and the ZAP baseline for a URL. Their findings go into the same report and SARIF, each labelled with the tool, its version and its rule. Nothing is downloaded or uploaded, and an area that neither Penthera's rules nor another tool reached is reported as "not covered".

penthera giants              # which tools you have
penthera --repo . --giants   # Penthera, then each installed tool

This runs the tools you have and merges their findings. It is not a claim that the combination finds more: experiment E14 measured that (results). Details, safety rules and the policy key: docs/commands/giants.md.

Ethics and authorization

Penthera sends HTTP requests to the targets you give it, and some modes (--deep, --fuzz, --adaptive, --all) send attack payloads, after a confirmation. Scan only what you own, what you have written authorization to test, or local environments you control. Do not use it to probe third-party systems, exfiltrate data, disrupt services, or harm anyone. Unauthorized testing may break computer-misuse laws such as the US CFAA, the UK Computer Misuse Act, and their EU equivalents. When in doubt, do not scan.

The software is provided "as is", without warranty. The author accepts no liability for misuse, and you are responsible for making sure every scan you run is lawful. The live check on penthera.org has its own terms.

Releases are deliberately slow: a feature freeze, an independent review, the release checks, and a release candidate before any new minor version. Watch the repository for releases or join the Discussions.

How Penthera is built

Penthera is developed with substantial help from generative AI: 91% of the commits up to v1.7.0 were written with Claude (Anthropic) through Claude Code, directed and reviewed by the maintainer, and marked with an AI-Assisted: trailer. Generated code passes the same gates as any change: tests, CodeQL, an independent review, the internal audit, and a 2FA-approved release. Inside the product, models only ever propose; deterministic checks decide. The full disclosure, and the rules for AI-assisted contributions, are in docs/genai.md.

Contributing and support

Clone the repository and run npm install, then npm test for the suite and npm run bench for precision and recall. CONTRIBUTING.md covers the project layout, the release cadence and the release checklist; AGENTS.md is the short version for coding agents. The roadmap shows what ships next, and the research plan what we measure. Issues and pull requests are welcome.

Penthera is free and stays free. If it caught something before you shipped it, you can sponsor its maintenance. Sponsorship pays for maintainer time and buys no influence over findings (tiers).

Daily notes from Penthera: x.com/penthera_org

Who builds it: Daan van der Zwaag, part-time and in the open.

How it compares: next to Snyk, Socket, Semgrep, ZAP and GitHub.

132 readable rules · 6 read-only MCP tools · 0 runtime dependencies · 0 requests past loopback in the benchmark · MIT, no telemetry

它是什么

Penthera checks your app, its dependencies and your AI coding tools on your own machine. It fixes what it can, with your approval. Every finding comes from a rule you can read, with its evidence at file:line. A model may propose; a rule decides.

It is also an open R&D project. We measure every check in public and publish the results, good or bad, so you can see how far to trust it.

It finds known classes of problems, not novel ones. It does not replace a human pentester.

Start in 30 seconds

You need Node.js 22 or later. No install, no account.

Building with Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, VS Code, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, Zed, JetBrains or Kiro, or an app builder such as Lovable, Bolt, Base44, Replit or v0? Penthera in your coding tool has the setup for each.

In your terminal. Run this in your project folder:

npx penthera

It detects your setup offline, asks what to check, and gives you a grade per area and the three things to fix first. It scans your running app only after you confirm the app is yours. Nothing is committed or pushed (guided start).

How it is measured

Each feature goes through the same path: method → evidence → tool.

  • Method. The methodology states the threat model, what black-box (HTTP) and white-box (source) analysis can and cannot see, the confidence model, and the false-positive controls on each probe. Each design choice cites the research or standard it rests on: 158 verified references, in APA style, in docs/references.md.
  • Evidence. A benchmark runs on every release, and the release gate fails if precision or recall drops by more than 0.02. Experiments that decide what ships next are pre-registered in docs/research/prereg/ before any data is collected, and the results are published either way.
  • Tool. What holds up ships in a reviewed, signed release. What does not hold up is dropped, and the rules stay.

为什么您可以信任它

  • Local and offline. No account, no telemetry, no cloud. --offline limits network traffic to the target you named, and every report lists the hosts it contacted (network use).
  • Tested unplugged. Repo scans, agents, deps, brief, evidence bundles and URL scans with --offline made no outside connections. They gave the same result twice, and the same with the network blocked, on macOS and Ubuntu (E17 results). The test can't watch git, which Penthera uses only for local commands.
  • 确定性的。 Rules you can read, with file:line evidence. A model may propose a fix or a lead; a deterministic re-scan and your tests decide.
  • Non-destructive by default. Default scans send no attack payloads. Payload testing (--deep, --fuzz, --adaptive, --all) is opt-in, asks for a confirmation bound to the target, and is rate-limited. It can change data, so read what active modes can change first.
  • Asks before it changes anything. The fix loop works on a local branch, asks before every change by default, and never pushes or opens pull requests.
  • No update channel to hijack. Detection rules ship inside reviewed releases as signed, versioned rule packs. You can add your own by path (--rules <dir>). Nothing is downloaded and run at run time.
  • Releases you can verify. npm provenance through trusted publishing, a maintainer approval with 2FA for every version, SHA-pinned CI, CodeQL and OpenSSF Scorecard. Every release passes an internal audit of eight gates (latest report).

Run the free tools you already have: --giants

--giants runs the free scanners installed on your machine after Penthera's own scan: gitleaks, TruffleHog, Semgrep with your local rules, osv-scanner, Trivy and Checkov for a repository, nuclei and the ZAP baseline for a URL. Their findings go into the same report and SARIF, each labelled with the tool, its version and its rule. Nothing is downloaded or uploaded, and an area that neither Penthera's rules nor another tool reached is reported as "not covered".

penthera giants              # which tools you have
penthera --repo . --giants   # Penthera, then each installed tool

This runs the tools you have and merges their findings. It is not a claim that the combination finds more: experiment E14 measured that (results). Details, safety rules and the policy key: docs/commands/giants.md.

Ethics and authorization

Penthera sends HTTP requests to the targets you give it, and some modes (--deep, --fuzz, --adaptive, --all) send attack payloads, after a confirmation. Scan only what you own, what you have written authorization to test, or local environments you control. Do not use it to probe third-party systems, exfiltrate data, disrupt services, or harm anyone. Unauthorized testing may break computer-misuse laws such as the US CFAA, the UK Computer Misuse Act, and their EU equivalents. When in doubt, do not scan.

The software is provided "as is", without warranty. The author accepts no liability for misuse, and you are responsible for making sure every scan you run is lawful. The live check on penthera.org has its own terms.

Inside the product, models only ever propose; deterministic checks decide. The full disclosure, and the rules for AI-assisted contributions, are in docs/genai.md.
